%c[255,170,220,255]Order board%c[default]
The Orders section is open in the PDA from the start of the game. Up to five offers are posted on the board and refresh independently as in-game time passes. Orders for cooked artefacts become available as you learn the corresponding recipes.

%c[255,120,210,120]Accepting an order%c[default]
No more than five orders can be active at the same time. An accepted offer appears among active tasks. The nearest available delivery point on the current level is selected and marked on the map. After a delivery, that point cannot be assigned to a new order for one in-game hour. Orders cannot be accepted while the delivery network is offline; its status is shown above the list.

%c[255,255,190,90]Delivering the shipment%c[default]
Collect every listed item and keep it in the backpack. Equipped and belted items do not count toward the order. Approach the marked container and press the use key; eligible cargo is transferred automatically.

%c[255,235,105,90]Deadline and payment%c[default]
The deadline uses in-game time. After an on-time delivery, the client transfers the reward automatically one in-game day later.

%c[255,235,105,90]An expired order closes without payment.%c[default]

%c[255,170,220,255]Repair kits%c[default]
Weapon and armor repair kits have two charges each. Use RMB to choose suitable gear from the inventory or drag the kit onto the desired item. The armor kit also repairs helmets.

%c[255,120,210,120]Effect: up to +20 percentage points of condition per charge.%c[default]
A repair kit works at 20% condition or higher, but below 90%, and cannot raise condition above 90%.

%c[255,255,190,90]Metal part%c[default]
It works only on a weapon displaying 90–99% condition. It adds 2 percentage points, up to a maximum of 100%, and is consumed after the repair.

%c[255,170,220,255]Application%c[default]
Use a single-use field kit through RMB or drag it onto a weapon.

%c[255,255,190,90]Limit: no more than three field modifications per weapon.%c[default]

Specialized magazine, reload, caliber and weight kits can each be installed only once on a particular weapon.

%c[255,170,220,255]Application%c[default]
The disassembly kit has five charges. Use RMB to choose gear or drag it onto a weapon, outfit or helmet.

%c[255,235,105,90]Warning: the selected item will be destroyed.%c[default]

%c[255,120,210,120]Results%c[default]
A weapon yields a metal part and its last non-unique upgrade, if any. Its unique anomalous upgrade is always recovered as well, regardless of installation order. A helmet may yield a filter, while an outfit yields reusable protective components.

The result for a particular item remains stable across saving and loading.

%c[255,170,220,255]Discharge%c[default]
An active detector gradually drains its charge. The PDA warns at 25%, and an empty detector switches off. A stowed device does not drain its battery.

A full charge provides 90 minutes of active use for the Echo, 60 for the Bear, 45 for the Veles, and 30 for the Svarog. For stash metal detectors, the Homemade lasts 60 minutes, the Wave 45, and the Magnet 30. These are minutes of active device operation, not hours on the in-game calendar.

%c[255,120,210,120]Krona battery: +15 minutes of operation.%c[default]
It charges both device families. Drag the battery onto a detector or select the desired device through RMB. Charge cannot exceed full capacity.

%c[255,255,190,90]Disassembly%c[default]
Use RMB to disassemble a detector into electronic parts. The Echo and Homemade yield 1–3 parts; the Bear and Wave yield 2–4; the Veles and Magnet yield 3–5. The Svarog yields five different materials, one of each kind.

%c[255,170,220,255]How to search%c[default]
In Pripyat, hold a metal detector. Its beeps accelerate as you approach a hidden stash.

%c[255,210,210,210]Homemade:%c[default] %c[255,130,220,120]green — 30 m%c[default], %c[255,100,205,235]cyan — 20 m%c[default].

%c[255,210,210,210]Wave:%c[default] %c[255,100,205,235]cyan — 20 m%c[default], %c[255,190,140,230]purple — 10 m%c[default].

%c[255,210,210,210]Magnetic:%c[default] %c[255,100,205,235]cyan — 25 m%c[default], %c[255,190,140,230]purple — 20 m%c[default], %c[255,255,170,80]orange — 5 m%c[default]. Discovered orange stashes are marked on the map.

%c[255,170,220,255]Deployment%c[default]
Use the field backpack to create a personal stash marked on the map.

%c[255,255,190,90]GPS tracker%c[default]
Place a GPS tracker inside your personal stash to show its contents in the PDA marker tooltip. Without a GPS, the backpack marker remains, but no item list is shown.

A GPS can also be placed in a vehicle trunk. When the engine is off, a vehicle marker appears with the trunk contents. The marker is hidden while the engine is running and returns when the engine is switched off. Removing the last GPS removes the vehicle marker.

%c[255,120,210,120]Automatic folding%c[default]
When the last item is taken from the personal stash, the empty backpack folds and returns to the inventory. A GPS left inside also counts as an item.

%c[255,170,220,255]Sleeping bag%c[default]
Opens the native Call of Pripyat sleep dialog and is not consumed.

%c[255,255,190,90]Sleeping pills%c[default]
Open the same sleep dialog but are consumed after one use.

%c[255,170,220,255]How wear occurs%c[default]
Belted artefacts lose condition while restoring actor parameters or absorbing damage.

%c[255,255,190,90]Useful effects weaken as condition falls.%c[default]
Condition does not drop below the engine's safe minimum.

%c[255,170,220,255]Installation%c[default]
A placed radio beacon appears on the map. Hovering shows distance, travel time, and expected equipment wear.

%c[255,120,210,120]Fast travel%c[default]
Travel time depends on distance: roughly 30 in-game minutes per 500 meters, or one in-game hour per kilometer. The minimum is one in-game minute, and the maximum is six hours.

Weapons, armor, helmets, and detectors in the inventory wear down during travel, including gear in the backpack. Wear depends on distance and varies slightly around the displayed estimate for each item. Artefacts do not wear out during travel.

%c[255,255,190,90]Anomalous boots%c[default]
Worn on the belt, they reduce travel equipment wear by 70%, leaving 30% of the normal wear. They have no effect in the backpack. Multiple pairs do not increase the bonus.

%c[255,235,105,90]Travel is unavailable while bleeding or above 100 mSv radiation.%c[default]

A beacon withstands 5–10 ordinary hits. Two knife strikes are enough to destroy it.

%c[255,170,220,255]PDA hacking: how to play%c[default] 
Your goal is to fill hacking progress to 100% before you run out of scripts. Everything uses the mouse: there is no need to type commands. 

%c[255,120,210,120][1] Action points — actions%c[default] 
This is your supply of moves. An ordinary hack costs 1 point. Attempting an additional purple stash costs 2 points, legendary costs 3, and red costs 4. 
Exception: ./recover-actions adds points without spending any, but uses up one script. Zero actions does not mean you have lost: as long as you have a script, you can recover actions. 

%c[255,120,210,120][2] Scripts — the left list, /mnt/usb/payloads%c[default] 
Each script contains a set of hacks. Click a script to see its hacks. You can browse different scripts freely: selecting one does not spend anything. 
The number by the script name is its power. The number of remaining scripts is shown separately in the payloads counter. If you run out of scripts while progress is still below 100%, the hack is lost. 

%c[255,120,210,120][3] Hacks — the command list with [RUN]%c[default] 
Clicking a hack runs it immediately, without a second confirmation. You get its effect, then the selected script disappears along with all of its hacks. 
%c[255,255,190,90]One script = one executed hack. You cannot run every hack in a single script.%c[default] 
This also applies to recovering actions, obtaining new scripts, and failed trace attempts. If you lack the required action points, the command does not run and the script remains. 

%c[255,120,210,120][4] PDA protection — the crypto.lock bar%c[default] 
Lower protection makes ./decrypt add more progress and improves the chance of additional stashes. ./weaken lowers protection, but does not fill progress itself. You do not have to lower protection all the way to zero. 

%c[255,120,210,120][5] Hacking progress — the /dev/pda0 bar%c[default] 
Fill this bar to 100%. The main command for this is ./decrypt. The +…% beside it shows how much progress it will add right now. 

%c[255,170,220,255]A simple sequence%c[default] 
1. Browse the scripts on the left and compare their hacks. 
2. Watch your supplies: ./recover-actions restores actions, while ./rescan-usb provides new scripts. Getting new scripts costs 1 action, and the current script is still consumed. Do not wait until no scripts remain to replenish them. 
3. If protection is high and you have enough resources, consider ./weaken. Then choose ./decrypt to raise progress. After each command, the next script is selected; it will have a different set of hacks. 
4. Keep replenishing supplies as needed and decrypting until you reach 100%. For example, at 85% progress, ./decrypt +16% will finish the hack. 
5. Extra stashes and money are optional. Learn to finish a normal hack first: bonus commands spend scripts you may need to win. 

The center contains a log of executed actions. [?] opens help. The extracts counter shows remaining money extraction attempts, not your supply of moves. 

%c[255,255,190,90]Other commands and additional stashes%c[default] 
./extract-wallet grants money immediately without adding progress. ./brute-boot attempts an instant win at the displayed chance; failure adds no progress but spends the action and script. The rare ./skeleton-key completes the hack immediately, but inflicts a psy-hit. 

./trace-purple, ./trace-legendary, and ./trace-red attempt to intercept additional coordinates. The percentage is the success chance; [-N] is the action point cost. Each of the three trace tiers allows one attempt per PDA. Weaken protection before attempting a trace: further weakening cannot restore a failed attempt. Even after a successful trace, you must finish the hack at 100% to receive its coordinates. Reloading alone does not reroll a particular PDA. 

%c[255,170,220,255]Preparation and reward%c[default] 
Install USB software through RMB: the USB is consumed, but access remains permanently. USB-1 unlocks Novice and Stalker PDAs, USB-2 unlocks Veteran PDAs, and USB-3 unlocks Master PDAs. 
A successful hack grants the basic lead for the PDA rank: Novice — green, Stalker — cyan, Veteran — purple, Master — guaranteed legendary. Successful extra traces are granted with it. The PDA is consumed after coordinates are successfully granted. 

%c[255,235,105,90]Losing or manually leaving the hacking window locks the PDA.%c[default] 

%c[255,255,190,90]Reflashing and unlocking%c[default] 
Apply a Reflashing Module to a locked PDA through RMB. It immediately grants the basic lead for that rank without a minigame or additional traces. A Master PDA guarantees a legendary lead. The module and PDA are consumed after coordinates are successfully granted. 
Nitro can restore a locked PDA to working order for a fee. This does not grant coordinates: you must still hack the unlocked PDA normally.

%c[255,235,105,90]Warning%c[default]
Using strange food or drink causes a blackout.
